t.5.58.2: Now that the matter has come to this pass and has been reported to you, it would be fitting for us to go and see those two sons of the king together with Vaidehī.
t.5.58.1: Having heard those words of his, the son of Vālin, after seeking the leave of all the great monkeys headed by Jāmbavant, spoke.
t.5.58.3: Even I alone am sufficient to swiftly destroy that city of Laṅkā together with its hosts of Rākṣasas, and Rāvaṇa of great might as well.
t.5.58.4: How much more, then, when I am joined by you, heroic monkeys who are mighty, self-possessed, skilled in weapons, capable and eager for victory!
t.5.58.5: But I, in battle, will destroy Rāvaṇa together with his army and his vanguard, together with his son and accompanied by his brothers, in the fight.
t.5.58.6: Even if the missiles of Śakrajit in battle, the Brāhma, the Aindra, the Raudra, the Vāyavya and likewise the Vāruṇa, are hard to look upon, I shall blow them away and I shall slay the Rākṣasas.
t.5.58.7: With your permission, my valor will hold him in check.
t.5.58.8: For an incomparable, unceasing shower of rocks released by me would slay even the gods in battle; how much more, then, those night-rovers?
t.5.58.9: The ocean might overstep its shore, and Mandara itself might totter, but no enemy host could make Jāmbavant tremble in battle.
t.5.58.11: By the mighty thrust of the thighs of Panasa and of the great-souled Nīla even Mount Mandara would be shattered to pieces; how much more, then, the Rākṣasas in battle!
t.5.58.10: The heroic monkey, the son of Vāyu, is alone enough for the destruction of all the hosts of rākṣasas, and of those rākṣasas who stand foremost among them.
t.5.58.12: Among the gods, asuras, gandharvas, serpents and birds, even in their battles, tell me: who is there to stand against Mainda in combat, or against Dvivida?
t.5.58.13: These two sons of the Aśvins, of great swiftness and foremost among monkeys, have assumed supreme arrogance from the pride of Pitāmaha's boon.
t.5.58.14: For long ago the Grandsire of all the worlds, out of regard for the Aśvins, granted these two an incomparable immunity from being slain by anyone.
t.5.58.15: Intoxicated with pride in the boon they had received, those two heroic monkeys crushed the mighty army of the gods and drank the nectar of immortality.
t.5.58.16: These two alone, once enraged, are able to destroy Laṅkā together with its horses, chariots and elephants; let all the other vānaras stand aside.
t.5.58.17: But, O monkeys, it is not proper for us, having seen her, to go into the presence of the great-souled Rāghava without the queen.
t.5.58.18: To report there, "The queen was seen but not brought back," seems to me unfitting for you, whose valour is renowned.
t.5.58.19: For in all the worlds, including the immortals and the Daityas, there is no one equal to you in leaping, nor anyone equal to you in valour, O best of monkeys.
t.5.58.20: Now that the rākṣasas have thus had their heroes slain by Hanumān, what else remains to be done here? Let us take Jānakī and go.
t.5.58.21: To him, who had thus made his resolve, Jāmbavān, the best of the monkeys, who knew what was fitting, spoke, supremely pleased, words full of meaning.
t.5.58.22: O prince, this resolve of ours, as you see it, is certainly not unfitting; but you should regard the accomplishment of the task in the way that Rāma's mind is set upon it.
